exposure: Twin pregnancy with a live fetus and a hydatidiform mole
outcome: Maternal complications (bleeding, anemia, blood transfusion, threatening miscarriage, pre-eclampsia)
End-of-gestation outcomes (living and healthy newborns, dead babies)
cohort: Twelve cases of twin molar pregnancies with a single viable fetus, identified from obstetric reports over 20 years at a Maternity and Pediatrics Teaching Hospital.
finding: This study describes the clinical presentation and outcomes of 12 rare cases of twin molar pregnancies with a live viable fetus, highlighting maternal complications and end-of-gestation outcomes including five living and healthy newborns and three dead babies.
mod_finding: Cesarean sections were documented as an end-of-gestation outcome in these cases.
gest_age: Average gestational age at delivery commencement was 26.67 ± 7.09 weeks, ranging from 17 to 35 weeks.
